pages.text: The morning market bustled. Lots of fish had arrived at Mom's stall.
They wanted to help lay out the fish. Mom dipped her hand into the salt tub before picking up a fish.
Lolo plunged both hands into the basin. Riri looked for the biggest fish first. "Just move them quickly." "Big ones first will look nice."
Lolo gathered an armful of fish. The slippery fish slid free.
Plop, plop, they fell back into the basin. Lolo's arms were empty.
Riri put a big fish at the front. When a bigger one appeared, she changed their places again.
After moving them again and again, everything was mixed up. Beads of sweat dotted Riri's forehead.
Riri looked at Mom's hands. White salt covered them.
They put salt on their hands too. Now the fish stayed firmly in their grip instead of slipping.
Fish lay side by side in front of the stall. Lolo wiped their forehead with a salty hand. Seeing it turn white, Mom giggled.
